video_title: Jason Kidd Reflects on His Nets Legacy, Favorite Teammates & the NBA’s Best Passers of All Time

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on his trade to the New Jersey Nets
quotes.excerpt: when I got traded from Phoenix to New Jersey to the Nets, everybody was I think shocked.
quotes.quote: When I got traded from Phoenix to New Jersey to the Nets, everybody was I think shocked. I was shocked, but I was excited because I had the opportunity to go East. When you talk about basketball, a lot of times, basketball is king on the East and the West Coast is forgotten. Knowing the Nets didn't have success before I got there, to be able to help them be successful, I made a prediction, I think it was just to be .500, 41 and 41, and the media thought that was funny, but that was just being average.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on missing out on a championship with the Nets
quotes.excerpt: I always think about coming up short because we had two opportunities to win a title.
quotes.quote: I always think about coming up short because we had two opportunities to win a title. Maybe not that first year, but the second year we definitely did.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on changing the culture of the Nets
quotes.excerpt: I knew a couple players. I knew Luc Longley, as I played with him in Dallas.
quotes.quote: Maybe being a little bold, but I thought I knew a couple players. I knew Luc Longley, as I played with him in Dallas. I had someone that I knew, I knew he could play, I knew he could make shots, and he understood who I was. So I thought if I make this prediction, he would help. And then understanding I knew Richard Jefferson. Drafted with the trade to get RJ and Kenyon Martin, I said, 'Oh, we got some West Coast players,' so I thought they could help. They did more than help, they definitely were a part of that foundation.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on the importance of team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: losing can become the norm. And so understanding we were getting healthy.
quotes.quote: Losing can become the norm. And so understanding we were getting healthy. There were some healthy parts that were coming and I got I think lucky. Kerry Kittles is coming back, we get Kenyon Martin, understanding that rookie class that Rod Thorn drafted. Also, we all had a chip on our shoulder. We all wanted not to be the laughing stock or the bottom of the barrel or a layover sort of call when teams come and go. This is just a quick stop, we'll get a win and we move on. So those ingredients turned out to help us win.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on his favorite teammates on the Nets
quotes.excerpt: I'm not the guy who's going to dominate the ball, the score.
quotes.quote: I'm not the guy who's going to dominate the ball, the score. So when you talk about scores and guys who can get out and run, Kenyon Martin, Richard Jefferson, Kerry Kittles. I love Brian Scalabrine and the energy that he brought. He was part of that rookie class, that freshman class I call it. Those guys worked extremely hard, they all wanted to win, they were all winners in their college programs.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on Kenyon Martin as a teammate
quotes.excerpt: Kenyon Martin, a loyal soldier, not afraid of anything, super athletic, made me look good.
quotes.quote: Kenyon Martin, a loyal soldier, not afraid of anything, super athletic, made me look good. Caught a lot of balls that were probably going out of bounds, and then also just his energy and his toughness, he was one of our leaders.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on Richard Jefferson as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: a pro. When you talk about a rookie, he wanted to be good.
quotes.quote: A pro. When you talk about a rookie, he wanted to be good. He worked extremely hard on his game. He would tell you that he wasn't a shooter when he came to the league, but when he left he was. But again, another athlete, understood to run the right lane because that's what he was taught at Arizona. Being able to get the ball to him and it was going to be a layup, dunk, or free throws, and he was really good at that as a rookie.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on Brian Scalabrine's role
quotes.excerpt: Brian Scalabrine, I think sometimes he flies on your radar. I thought he was incredible for us.
quotes.quote: Brian Scalabrine, I think sometimes he flies on your radar. I thought he was incredible for us. He was an assassin, there wasn't any pressure on him. A guy that could play on the perimeter, could shoot it, put it on the floor for post-up. And then, I would say Anthony Johnson is one that probably doesn't get talked enough because he was my backup. He didn't get to play enough minutes. Maybe should have played more minutes, but I don't think he gets enough love for being on those teams.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on the team's mindset during the Finals
quotes.excerpt: it was about the team and we all took pride of playing defense.
quotes.quote: It was about the team and we all took pride of playing defense. We wanted to play fast, and we had fun. And so winning becomes contagious. We did end up losing, but I think that helped us for experience. We get back to the Finals, unfortunately again, not being able to win against San Antonio, but take it at the six games. We improved by two games and in that six game you actually had the lead and our offense and defense closed, but there in San Antonio took advantage of it.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on Vince Carter's impact
quotes.excerpt: he's a competitor. His numbers well-deserved to be in the rafters with the Nets.
quotes.quote: He's a competitor. His numbers well-deserved to be in the rafters with the Nets. When we got him, we were all excited that he was going to help us get to the finish line. And so as a teammate, he made the game easy. As a friend, he was incredible off the floor.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on his passing creativity
quotes.excerpt: sometimes we're taken away, so what does that mean? How can you figure out how to get the ball.
quotes.quote: Sometimes we're taken away, so what does that mean? How can you figure out how to get the ball to your teammate in a different way? And so off the glass is one, the bounce pass, the spin, throwing a pass without a spin, you know, sort of skips. So just, you know, sometimes you take your creativity from being outside throwing rocks, you know, trying to skip the rocks across the pond. You try to do that in the game.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on copying Magic Johnson's passing
quotes.excerpt: when you look at Magic and the no-look pass, being able to, you know, copy that.
quotes.quote: When you look at Magic and the no-look pass, being able to, you know, copy that. That was my idol and so can I copy that pass? Can I copy a half-court bounce pass that he, you know, I might have seen him do. As I started to get a little older, I started to play against Gary Payton and Brian Shaw, and those are two guys that I, you know, tried to, you know, emulate because G defensively was a wizard and B Shaw, his tempo and the way he played the position. So I got to see those guys up close, and tried to, you know, do some of the things that they could. I knew the one thing I couldn't do with G was talk, so I let that alone and left that to G. He was a professional at that.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on the success of his youth program
quotes.excerpt: the time, Kobe is working with his daughter, and so understanding the the accident takes place.
quotes.quote: The time, Kobe is working with his daughter, and so understanding the the accident takes place. And so I felt that, you know, can I how can I help? And so that's where the idea came from. We started the program seven years ago in the Bay Area. We now have had over 60 girls get, you know, the division one scholarships, and so it's been a lot of fun to see these young ladies grow, and then continue their path in college.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on his top five passers of all time
quotes.excerpt: he's done it for a long, long time and he's I don't know if his records will ever be broken.
quotes.quote: He's done it for a long, long time and he's I don't know if his records will ever be broken, passing or steals, and that would be John Stockton. The ability to control the game with the pass, he would be one. I would go with Jason Williams, like chocolate, his creativity. I enjoyed, I hated guarding him because I knew the ball was going to go somewhere. And so, but his creativity was something that was I had me in awe, so I would have him up there. Magic, I would go with Magic, because that was my idol and that's the one that I I tried to, you know, duplicate. Another one I would say is Steve Nash. We grew up together, so just his ability to again, understand the pass and his creativity, and his success. Two-time MVP, you know, just wasn't just, you know, scoring, but being able to set the table. Last, oh shoot, that's a good one. In today's game, I would I would have to go with the Joker, being able to throw it full court. And then, you know, just in offense, his ability to make others run and they know they have opportunity to get the ball.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on Steve Nash's passing ability
quotes.excerpt: another one I would say is Steve Nash. We grew up together, so just his ability.
quotes.quote: Another one I would say is Steve Nash. We grew up together, so just his ability to again, understand the pass and his creativity, and his success. Two-time MVP, you know, just wasn't just, you know, scoring, but being able to set the table.

quotes.speaker: Jason Kidd
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Kidd on the passing style of his top five
quotes.excerpt: they're all playing chess. They're all always moving the pieces, always moving the defense.
quotes.quote: They're all playing chess. They're all always moving the pieces, always moving the defense, and also I think when you listen to their teammates, they make the game easy. And so that's what those those five do at a very, very high level.
